sources.note: Nothing; repeats that a tablet listed 169 (sic) names of which 59 legible, most in an unknown language, possibly Shubrian; cites MacGinnis 2012 and the Cambridge news item.

sources.citation: University of Cambridge Research News (2012), 'Archaeologists discover lost language' (press release summarising MacGinnis 2012)
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. States the evidence is 'a single clay tablet.. essentially a list of the names of women'; 'Altogether around 60 names are preserved.. the great majority belong to a previously unidentified language'; hypotheses: Shubrian, Mushki, or Zagros deportees (western Iran).
